005package org.wpilib.command3;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Seconds;
008import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
009
010import java.util.ArrayList;
011import java.util.Arrays;
012import java.util.Collection;
013import java.util.List;
014import java.util.function.BooleanSupplier;
015import java.util.function.Consumer;
016import org.wpilib.command3.Scheduler.ScheduleResult;
017import org.wpilib.system.Timer;
018import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
019
020/**
021 * A coroutine object is injected into command's {@link Command#run(Coroutine)} method to allow
022 * commands to yield and compositions to run other commands. Commands are considered <i>bound</i> to
023 * a coroutine while they're scheduled; attempting to use a coroutine outside the command bound to
024 * it will result in an {@code IllegalStateException} being thrown.
025 */
026public final class Coroutine {
027  private final Scheduler m_scheduler;
028  private final Continuation m_backingContinuation;
029
030  private boolean m_cancelOnForkFailure = true;
031  private ForkResult m_lastForkFailure = null;
032  private boolean m_cancellationRequested = false;
033
034  /**
035   * Creates a new coroutine. Package-private; only the scheduler should be creating these.
036   *
037   * @param scheduler The scheduler running the coroutine
038   * @param scope The continuation scope the coroutine's backing continuation runs in
039   * @param callback The callback for the continuation to execute when mounted. Often a command
040   *     function's body.
041   */
042  Coroutine(Scheduler scheduler, ContinuationScope scope, Consumer<Coroutine> callback) {
043    m_scheduler = scheduler;
044    m_backingContinuation = new Continuation(scope, () -> callback.accept(this));
045  }
046
047  /**
048   * Configures the coroutine to cancel itself if a child command couldn't be forked. This setting
049   * defaults to {@code true}, but can be changed to allow the coroutine to continue running after a
050   * fork failure.
051   *
052   * <p>This setting only affects commands forked by using the coroutine methods {@code fork},
053   * {@code await}, {@code awaitAll}, or {@code awaitAny}. Commands scheduled directly with {@link
054   * Scheduler#schedule(Command)} or via inner trigger bindings will not be affected.
055   *
056   * @param cancelOnForkFailure true to make the coroutine cancel itself if a child command couldn't
057   *     be forked, false to allow the coroutine to continue running after a fork failure
058   * @see #fork(Command...)
059   * @see #fork(Collection)
060   * @see #await(Command)
061   * @see #awaitAll(Command...)
062   * @see #awaitAll(Collection)
063   * @see #awaitAny(Command...)
064   * @see #awaitAny(Collection)
065   */
066  public void setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean cancelOnForkFailure) {
067    m_cancelOnForkFailure = cancelOnForkFailure;
068  }
069
070  /**
071   * Checks if the coroutine is currently configured to cancel itself if a child command couldn't be
072   * forked.
073   *
074   * @return true if the coroutine will cancel itself if a child command couldn't be forked, false
075   *     otherwise
076   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
077   */
078  public boolean isCancelOnForkFailure() {
079    return m_cancelOnForkFailure;
080  }
081
082  // Package-private. User code can never access this because setting the flag happens immediately
083  // before the coroutine yields itself.
084  boolean isInterruptRequested() {
085    return m_cancelOnForkFailure && m_lastForkFailure != null;
086  }
087
088  /**
089   * Requests early cancellation of the coroutine and the command bound to it. Any child commands
090   * will be canceled as well, as commands can never outlive their parent, but the parent command
091   * will not be canceled.
092   *
093   * <p>Team code shouldn't need to use this; instead, use a {@code return} statement in your
094   * command's function body to exit early. This method is primarily to be used by internal APIs
095   * that don't have access to the command's function body.
096   */
097  public void requestCancellation() {
098    requireMounted();
099
100    // Set the flag and immediately yield. The scheduler will check the flag after the yield call
101    // and cancel the command and its descendants.
102    m_cancellationRequested = true;
103    this.yield();
104  }
105
106  // package-private; setting the flag will immediately yield, so user code can never access this
107  // in a state where it returns anything other than `false`
108  boolean isCancellationRequested() {
109    return m_cancellationRequested;
110  }
111
112  ForkResult getForkResult() {
113    return m_lastForkFailure;
114  }
115
116  /**
117   * Yields control back to the scheduler to allow other commands to execute. This can be thought of
118   * as "pausing" the currently executing command.
119   *
120   * @return true
121   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
122   */
123  public boolean yield() {
124    requireMounted();
125
126    return m_backingContinuation.yield();
127  }
128
129  /**
130   * Parks the current command. No code in a command declared after calling {@code park()} will be
131   * executed. A parked command will never complete naturally and must be interrupted or canceled.
132   *
133   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
134   */
135  @SuppressWarnings("InfiniteLoopStatement")
136  public void park() {
137    requireMounted();
138
139    while (true) {
140      // 'this' is required because 'yield' is a semi-keyword and needs to be qualified
141      this.yield();
142    }
143  }
144
145  /**
146   * Represents the result of a fork operation that attempts to schedule multiple commands
147   * concurrently. The class provides information about the success or failure of the fork operation
148   * as well as utility methods to handle the outcome.
149   *
150   * <p>Instances of this class are immutable and provide methods to access the details of the
151   * forked and failed commands.
152   */
153  public final class ForkResult {
154    private final List<? extends Command> m_forkedCommands;
155    private final List<? extends ScheduleResult.Failure> m_failedCommands;
156
157    // private - only the coroutine can construct these
158    private ForkResult(
159        Collection<? extends Command> forkedCommands,
160        List<? extends ScheduleResult.Failure> failedCommands) {
161      m_forkedCommands = List.copyOf(forkedCommands);
162      m_failedCommands = List.copyOf(failedCommands);
163    }
164
165    /**
166     * Checks if the fork request was successful.
167     *
168     * @return True if no commands failed to be forked, false if at least one failed.
169     */
170    public boolean successful() {
171      return m_failedCommands.isEmpty();
172    }
173
174    /**
175     * Checks if the fork request failed.
176     *
177     * @return True if at least one command failed to be forked, false if all commands were
178     *     successfully forked.
179     */
180    public boolean failed() {
181      return !successful();
182    }
183
184    /**
185     * Checks if the fork request was partially successful. A partial success is defined as at least
186     * one command being forked but at least one failing to be forked. This can happen if a child
187     * immediately schedules a grandchild with a higher priority than a later sibling that shares
188     * requirements with that grandchild.
189     *
190     * @return True if at least one command was forked but at least one failed to be forked, false
191     *     if all commands were successfully forked or none were forked.
192     */
193    public boolean partialSuccess() {
194      return !m_forkedCommands.isEmpty() && !m_failedCommands.isEmpty();
195    }
196
197    /**
198     * Waits for all forked commands to complete. Unlike a fork-then-await pattern, which will
199     * reschedule any forked commands that already completed, {@code awaitCompletion()} will only
200     * wait for the forked commands that are still running.
201     *
202     * <p>This method does nothing if no commands were successfully forked.
203     */
204    public void awaitCompletion() {
205      for (Command command : m_forkedCommands) {
206        if (m_scheduler.isRunning(command)) {
207          Coroutine.this.yield();
208        }
209      }
210    }
211
212    /**
213     * Returns the list of commands that failed to be forked. This list is read-only and cannot be
214     * modified.
215     *
216     * @return The list of failed commands.
217     */
218    public List<? extends ScheduleResult.Failure> getFailedCommands() {
219      return m_failedCommands;
220    }
221
222    /**
223     * Returns the list of commands that were successfully forked. This list is read-only and cannot
224     * be modified.
225     *
226     * @return The list of forked commands.
227     */
228    public List<? extends Command> getForkedCommands() {
229      return m_forkedCommands;
230    }
231  }
232
233  /**
234   * Checks that all the given commands can be forked.
235   *
236   * @param commands The commands to check
237   * @return A failure-type ForkResult if the commands can't all be scheduled, or null on success.
238   */
239  private ForkResult checkAllForkable(Collection<? extends Command> commands) {
240    // Check for user error; there's no reason to fork conflicting commands simultaneously
241    // Because this is a bug in user code, throw an error instead of returning a failure result
242    ConflictDetector.throwIfConflicts(commands);
243
244    var schedulable = new ArrayList<Command>();
245    var unschedulable = new ArrayList<ScheduleResult.Failure>();
246    for (var command : commands) {
247      var result = m_scheduler.isSchedulable(command);
248      if (result instanceof ScheduleResult.Failure fail) {
249        unschedulable.add(fail);
250      } else {
251        schedulable.add(command);
252      }
253    }
254
255    var result = new ForkResult(schedulable, unschedulable);
256    if (!unschedulable.isEmpty()) {
257      if (m_cancelOnForkFailure) {
258        // Canceling on fork failure means no coroutine or user code gets to run to handle the
259        // failure result
260        m_lastForkFailure = result;
261        this.yield();
262        // could throw an IllegalStateException, but probably shouldn't crash user code
263        return result;
264      } else {
265        // always return the failure object if self-cancellation is disabled
266        return result;
267      }
268    }
269
270    return result;
271  }
272
273  /**
274   * Performs the actual fork operation for a collection of commands. This is used in conjunction
275   * with {@link #checkAllForkable(Collection)} in case a child forks a grandchild that conflicts
276   * with another entry in the set.
277   *
278   * <p>Given this setup, child1 and child2 are both forkable at the same time (no shared
279   * requirements and no conflicts with running commands), but child1 immediately forks a higher
280   * priority command than child2, which prevents child2 from being scheduled.
281   *
282   * <pre>{@code
283   * parent:
284   *   child1:
285   *     fork priority(1000, mech)
286   *   child2: priority(0, mech))
287   * }</pre>
288   *
289   * @param commands The commands to fork
290   * @return A failure result if at least one of the given commands was unable to be scheduled, or a
291   *     success result if all commands were scheduled.
292   */
293  private ForkResult doFork(Collection<? extends Command> commands) {
294    var successes = new ArrayList<Command>();
295    var fails = new ArrayList<ScheduleResult.Failure>();
296    for (var command : commands) {
297      var result = m_scheduler.schedule(command);
298      if (result instanceof ScheduleResult.Failure fail) {
299        fails.add(fail);
300      } else {
301        successes.add(command);
302      }
303    }
304    ForkResult result = new ForkResult(successes, fails);
305
306    if (!fails.isEmpty() && m_cancelOnForkFailure) {
307      // At least one of the commands couldn't be scheduled due to runtime behavior that can't be
308      // checked ahead of time by `checkAllForkable`.
309      //
310      // We can't roll back the partial success; the commands that successfully started will have
311      // already affected the state of the robot and may have interrupted previously running
312      // commands, which we can't restore. The two options are to either cancel the entire command
313      // composition - which is the default behavior - or to allow user code to handle the failure
314      // and do something with it (eg trying something else, retrying, etc).
315      m_lastForkFailure = result;
316      this.yield();
317      return result; // note: unreachable
318    }
319
320    return result;
321  }
322
323  /**
324   * Schedules child commands and then immediately returns. The child commands will run until their
325   * natural completion, the parent command exits, or the parent command cancels it.
326   *
327   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
328   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
329   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
330   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
331   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
332   *
333   * <p>This is a nonblocking operation. To fork and then wait for the child command to complete,
334   * use {@link #await(Command)}.
335   *
336   * <p>The parent command will continue executing while the child command runs, and can resync with
337   * the child command using {@link #await(Command)}.
338   *
339   * <pre>{@code
340   * Command example() {
341   *   return Command.noRequirements(coroutine -> {
342   *     Command child = ...;
343   *     ForkResult childTask = coroutine.fork(child);
344   *     // ... do more things
345   *     // then sync back up with the child command
346   *     if (childTask.successful()) {
347   *       childTask.awaitCompletion();
348   *     }
349   *   }).named("Example");
350   * }
351   * }</pre>
352   *
353   * @param commands The commands to fork.
354   * @return a result indicating whether the fork was successful or if the commands could not be
355   *     forked
356   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
357   * @see #await(Command)
358   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
359   */
360  public ForkResult fork(Command... commands) {
361    requireMounted();
362
363    requireNonNullParam(commands, "commands", "Coroutine.fork");
364    for (int i = 0; i < commands.length; i++) {
365      requireNonNullParam(commands[i], "commands[" + i + "]", "Coroutine.fork");
366    }
367
368    var forkableCheck = checkAllForkable(Arrays.asList(commands));
369    if (forkableCheck.failed()) {
370      return forkableCheck;
371    }
372
373    return doFork(Arrays.asList(commands));
374  }
375
376  /**
377   * Forks off some commands. Each command will run until its natural completion, the parent command
378   * exits, or the parent command cancels it. The parent command will continue executing while the
379   * forked commands run, and can resync with the forked commands using {@link
380   * #awaitAll(Collection)}.
381   *
382   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
383   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
384   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
385   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
386   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
387   *
388   * <pre>{@code
389   * Command example() {
390   *   return Command.noRequirements(coroutine -> {
391   *     Collection<Command> innerCommands = ...;
392   *     ForkResult childTask = coroutine.fork(innerCommands);
393   *     // ... do more things
394   *     // then sync back up with the inner commands
395   *     if (childTask.successful()) {
396   *       childTask.awaitCompletion();
397   *     }
398   *   }).named("Example");
399   * }
400   * }</pre>
401   *
402   * @param commands The commands to fork.
403   * @return a result indicating whether the fork was successful or if the commands could not be
404   *     forked
405   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
406   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
407   */
408  public ForkResult fork(Collection<? extends Command> commands) {
409    return fork(commands.toArray(Command[]::new));
410  }
411
412  /**
413   * Awaits completion of a command. If the command is not currently scheduled or running, it will
414   * be scheduled automatically. This is a blocking operation and will not return until the command
415   * completes or has been interrupted by another command scheduled by the same parent.
416   *
417   * <p>If the child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
418   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then it will not be scheduled and the method call will
419   * return a {@link ForkResult} containing the command. If the coroutine is configured to cancel on
420   * fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will not get a chance to handle
421   * the failure result.
422   *
423   * @param command the command to await
424   * @return a result indicating whether the await was successful or if the commands could not be
425   *     awaited
426   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
427   * @see #fork(Command...)
428   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
429   */
430  public ForkResult await(Command command) {
431    requireMounted();
432
433    requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "Coroutine.await");
434
435    var forkableCheck = checkAllForkable(List.of(command));
436    if (forkableCheck.failed()) {
437      return forkableCheck;
438    }
439
440    // Don't need doFork() because there's no chance of sibling conflicts
441    m_scheduler.schedule(command);
442
443    while (m_scheduler.isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
444      // If the command is a one-shot, then the schedule call will completely execute the command.
445      // There would be nothing to await
446      this.yield();
447    }
448
449    return new ForkResult(List.of(command), List.of());
450  }
451
452  /**
453   * Awaits completion of all given commands. If any command is not currently scheduled or running,
454   * it will be scheduled.
455   *
456   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
457   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
458   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
459   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
460   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
461   *
462   * @param commands the commands to await
463   * @return a result indicating whether the await was successful or if the commands could not be
464   *     awaited
465   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the commands conflict with each other
466   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
467   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
468   */
469  public ForkResult awaitAll(Collection<? extends Command> commands) {
470    requireMounted();
471
472    requireNonNullParam(commands, "commands", "Coroutine.awaitAll");
473    int i = 0;
474    for (Command command : commands) {
475      requireNonNullParam(command, "commands[" + i + "]", "Coroutine.awaitAll");
476      i++;
477    }
478
479    var forkableCheck = checkAllForkable(commands);
480    if (forkableCheck.failed()) {
481      return forkableCheck;
482    }
483
484    var forkResult = doFork(commands);
485    if (forkResult.failed()) {
486      return forkResult;
487    }
488
489    while (commands.stream().anyMatch(m_scheduler::isScheduledOrRunning)) {
490      this.yield();
491    }
492
493    return forkResult;
494  }
495
496  /**
497   * Awaits completion of all given commands. If any command is not currently scheduled or running,
498   * it will be scheduled.
499   *
500   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
501   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
502   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
503   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
504   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
505   *
506   * @param commands the commands to await
507   * @return a result indicating whether the await was successful or if the commands could not be
508   *     awaited
509   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the commands conflict with each other
510   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
511   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
512   */
513  public ForkResult awaitAll(Command... commands) {
514    return awaitAll(Arrays.asList(commands));
515  }
516
517  /**
518   * Awaits completion of any given commands. Any command that's not already scheduled or running
519   * will be scheduled. After any of the given commands complete, the rest will be canceled.
520   *
521   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
522   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
523   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
524   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
525   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
526   *
527   * @param commands the commands to await
528   * @return a result indicating whether the await was successful or if the commands could not be
529   *     awaited
530   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the commands conflict with each other
531   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
532   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
533   */
534  public ForkResult awaitAny(Collection<? extends Command> commands) {
535    requireMounted();
536
537    requireNonNullParam(commands, "commands", "Coroutine.awaitAny");
538    int i = 0;
539    for (Command command : commands) {
540      requireNonNullParam(command, "commands[" + i + "]", "Coroutine.awaitAny");
541      i++;
542    }
543
544    var forkableCheck = checkAllForkable(commands);
545    if (forkableCheck.failed()) {
546      return forkableCheck;
547    }
548
549    var forkResult = doFork(commands);
550    if (forkResult.failed()) {
551      return forkResult;
552    }
553
554    while (commands.stream().allMatch(m_scheduler::isScheduledOrRunning)) {
555      this.yield();
556    }
557
558    // At least one command exited; cancel the rest.
559    commands.forEach(m_scheduler::cancel);
560
561    return forkResult;
562  }
563
564  /**
565   * Awaits completion of any given commands. Any command that's not already scheduled or running
566   * will be scheduled. After any of the given commands completes, the rest will be canceled.
567   *
568   * <p>If any child command is unable to be scheduled per the contract of {@link
569   * Scheduler#isSchedulable(Command)}, then none of the commands will be scheduled and the method
570   * call will return a {@link ForkResult} containing the unschedulable commands. If the coroutine
571   * is configured to cancel on fork failure, then the coroutine will be canceled and user code will
572   * not get a chance to handle the failure result.
573   *
574   * @param commands the commands to await
575   * @return a result indicating whether the await was successful or if the commands could not be
576   *     awaited
577   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the commands conflict with each other
578   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
579   * @see #setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)
580   */
581  public ForkResult awaitAny(Command... commands) {
582    return awaitAny(Arrays.asList(commands));
583  }
584
585  /**
586   * Waits for some duration of time to elapse. Returns immediately if the given duration is zero or
587   * negative. Call this within a command or command composition to introduce a simple delay.
588   *
589   * <p>For example, a basic autonomous routine that drives straight for 5 seconds:
590   *
591   * <pre>{@code
592   * Command timedDrive() {
593   *   return drivebase.run(coroutine -> {
594   *     drivebase.tankDrive(1, 1);
595   *     coroutine.wait(Seconds.of(5));
596   *     drivebase.stop();
597   *   }).named("Timed Drive");
598   * }
599   * }</pre>
600   *
601   * <p>Note that the resolution of the wait period is equal to the period at which {@link
602   * Scheduler#run()} is called by the robot program. If using a 20 millisecond update period, the
603   * wait will be rounded up to the nearest 20 millisecond interval; in this scenario, calling
604   * {@code wait(Milliseconds.of(1))} and {@code wait(Milliseconds.of(19))} would have identical
605   * effects.
606   *
607   * <p>Very small loop times near the loop period are sensitive to the order in which commands are
608   * executed. If a command waits for 10 ms at the end of a scheduler cycle, and then all the
609   * commands that ran before it complete or exit, and then the next cycle starts immediately, the
610   * wait will be evaluated at the <i>start</i> of that next cycle, which occurred less than 10 ms
611   * later. Therefore, the wait will see not enough time has passed and only exit after an
612   * additional cycle elapses, adding an unexpected extra 20 ms to the wait time. This becomes less
613   * of a problem with smaller loop periods, as the extra 1-loop delay becomes smaller.
614   *
615   * @param duration the duration of time to wait
616   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
617   */
618  public void wait(Time duration) {
619    requireMounted();
620
621    requireNonNullParam(duration, "duration", "Coroutine.wait");
622
623    var timer = Timer.createStarted();
624    while (!timer.hasElapsed(duration.in(Seconds))) {
625      this.yield();
626    }
627  }
628
629  /**
630   * Represents the result of a call to {@link Coroutine#waitUntil(BooleanSupplier)} or {@link
631   * Coroutine#waitUntil(BooleanSupplier, Time)}.
632   */
633  public enum WaitResult {
634    /** A call to {@code waitUntil} has met its condition. */
635    CONDITION_MET {
636      @Override
637      public boolean timedOut() {
638        return false;
639      }
640    },
641    /** A call to {@link Coroutine#waitUntil(BooleanSupplier, Time)} has timed out. */
642    TIMED_OUT {
643      @Override
644      public boolean timedOut() {
645        return true;
646      }
647    },
648    ;
649
650    /**
651     * Checks if the wait has timed out.
652     *
653     * @return true if this result was a timeout, false if the condition was met without timing out.
654     */
655    public abstract boolean timedOut();
656  }
657
658  /**
659   * Yields until a condition is met. This method will <b>only</b> return once the condition is met;
660   * if the condition never becomes true or is delayed longer than you expect, this method will
661   * block indefinitely. {@link #waitUntil(BooleanSupplier, Time)} is an alternative that will only
662   * wait up until a maximum duration before exiting.
663   *
664   * @param condition The condition to wait for
665   * @return {@link WaitResult#CONDITION_MET}
666   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
667   * @see #waitUntil(BooleanSupplier, Time)
668   */
669  public WaitResult waitUntil(BooleanSupplier condition) {
670    requireMounted();
671
672    requireNonNullParam(condition, "condition", "Coroutine.waitUntil");
673
674    while (!condition.getAsBoolean()) {
675      this.yield();
676    }
677
678    return WaitResult.CONDITION_MET;
679  }
680
681  /**
682   * Yields until a condition is met, waiting for up to a specified duration. If the condition is
683   * not met before the timeout duration elapses, this method stops waiting and returns {@link
684   * WaitResult#TIMED_OUT}.
685   *
686   * <p>Teams may use this method for waiting for conditions in autonomous or automated routines to
687   * be resilient to hardware faults (e.g., a mechanism not reaching a target state or a faulty
688   * sensor).
689   *
690   * <pre>{@code
691   * Command.noRequirements(coroutine -> {
692   *   coroutine.fork(elevator.up());
693   *   Coroutine.WaitResult upResult = coroutine.waitUntil(elevator::atTop, Seconds.of(1.25));
694   *   if (upResult.timedOut()) {
695   *     // We've waited 1.25 seconds and the elevator still has not reached the top. It may have
696   *     // jammed or there may be a fault with the sensors. In this example, we set a driverstation
697   *     // alert and exit early - team code may want to take other approaches like retrying the
698   *     // command or falling back to a secondary behavior that doesn't need the elevator to be up.
699   *     elevator.setJamAlert();
700   *     return;
701   *   }
702   *
703   *   // The elevator reached the top within 1.25 seconds. Clear the alert and continue.
704   *   elevator.clearJamAlert();
705   *
706   *   // ... more commands ...
707   * })
708   * }</pre>
709   *
710   * @param condition The condition to wait for
711   * @param timeout The maximum duration to wait
712   * @return {@link WaitResult#CONDITION_MET} if the condition was met within the specified timeout,
713   *     or {@link WaitResult#TIMED_OUT} if the timeout duration elapsed before the condition was
714   *     met.
715   * @see #waitUntil(BooleanSupplier)
716   */
717  public WaitResult waitUntil(BooleanSupplier condition, Time timeout) {
718    requireMounted();
719
720    requireNonNullParam(condition, "condition", "Coroutine.waitUntil");
721    requireNonNullParam(timeout, "timeout", "Coroutine.waitUntil");
722
723    var timer = Timer.createStarted();
724
725    while (!condition.getAsBoolean()) {
726      if (timer.hasElapsed(timeout)) {
727        return WaitResult.TIMED_OUT;
728      } else {
729        this.yield();
730      }
731    }
732
733    return WaitResult.CONDITION_MET;
734  }
735
736  /**
737   * Advanced users only: this permits access to the backing command scheduler to run custom logic
738   * not provided by the standard coroutine methods. Any commands manually scheduled through this
739   * will be canceled when the parent command exits - it's not possible to "fork" a command that
740   * lives longer than the command that scheduled it.
741   *
742   * @return the command scheduler backing this coroutine
743   * @throws IllegalStateException if called anywhere other than the coroutine's running command
744   */
745  public Scheduler scheduler() {
746    requireMounted();
747
748    return m_scheduler;
749  }
750
751  private boolean isMounted() {
752    return m_backingContinuation.isMounted();
753  }
754
755  private void requireMounted() {
756    // Note: attempting to yield() outside a command will already throw an error due to the
757    // continuation being unmounted, but other actions like forking and awaiting should also
758    // throw errors. For consistent messaging, we use this helper in all places, not just the
759    // ones that interact with the backing continuation.
760
761    if (isMounted()) {
762      return;
763    }
764
765    throw new IllegalStateException("Coroutines can only be used by the command bound to them");
766  }
767
768  // Package-private for interaction with the scheduler.
769  // These functions are not intended for team use.
770
771  void runToYieldPoint() {
772    m_backingContinuation.run();
773  }
774
775  void mount() {
776    Continuation.mountContinuation(m_backingContinuation);
777  }
778
779  boolean isDone() {
780    return m_backingContinuation.isDone();
781  }
782}
